items.note: Passive liquid-helium dewar (LN2-cooled shield) that the user fills with LN2 and LHe; it has no powered cooldown. IRLabs product page and brochure give only LN2/LHe hold times, no room-temperature-to-base cooldown time.
Passive LN2 dewar filled by the user; no cooldown concept. IRLabs documents give only static hold times.

LN2-immersed heated copper block. The cryostat cools when immersed in LN2 and is then controlled to the set point. Neither the Isotech data sheet (p.79), the product page nor the user manual (Instrumart-hosted Cryostat-459-Manual.pdf) gives a time to reach a set point. The manual only says to wait for everything to stabilise.

Simple LN2 boiling-point apparatus: the equalising block sits in a user-filled LN2 dewar at the nitrogen boiling point. There is no powered cooldown. The data sheet gives only the topping-up interval (about every 30 minutes) and readings 10 minutes after topping up, which is not a cooldown time.

LN2-cooled argon triple-point apparatus. The 2025 data sheet claims a 'Faster Time to Fixed Point Plateau' and a plateau lasting about 4 hours, but it gives no time to reach the plateau from room temperature. Neither the product page nor the 2018 seminar gives one either.

The JULABO MS-1000FF product page has a 'Cool-down time' section (medium: ethanol), but the data is only a chart image (chart-cd-magio-1000ff.webp). It cannot be quoted from text and was not read off the image. Neither JULABO USA nor the press release states a figure.

items.note: 3P55 cooldown to base (< 50 mK) is < 4 h, so the value is 4 h. The table columns read in order 0P55, 1P55, 2P55, 3P55. The sheet says specifications are guaranteed with wiring, standard options and integrations. The product page also gives '< 4 hrs Sample loading and cooldown to base'.
The LACO product page for X-1P33891 lists LN2 cooling, a temperature range and vacuum specs but no cooldown or pull-down time for the platen or shroud. No other LACO source found states one.
The LACO product page for X-1P33958 gives the -150 C rating, but no cooldown or pull-down time. No other LACO source found states one.

Neither the Lake Shore CCS-CP product page nor the large-sample-space datasheet (ccr-large-sample-space.pdf) gives a cooldown time. Cooldown times quoted for other Lake Shore CCS models do not apply to this configuration.

items.note: The datasheet gives the time to 5 K with LHe flow, not to the 3.5 K base, and states it as approximate (~30 min). Key features also say 'Fast cooldown — 30 min to 5 K'.
